name: Brandberg
kurzbeschreibung: Highest-lying village in the Zillertal, surrounded by untouched nature and stunning hiking trails in the Naturpark Zillertaler Alpen.
beschreibung:
Overview

Brandberg is an authentic mountain village in the upper Zillertal within the Schwaz district, perched at roughly 1,082 meters above sea level on a sunny terrace above the entrance to the Zillergrund valley. With around 380 inhabitants, it is one of the smallest residential communities in the valley, yet its municipal territory covers over 156 square kilometers, making it one of the largest in Tyrol as it stretches deep into the High Alps Nature Park Zillertal Alps all the way to the South Tyrolean border. Revered as the sunniest village in the valley, Brandberg sits high above bustling Mayrhofen. Steep mountain hay meadows, centuries-old wooden farmsteads, and serene alpine quietude define this unspoiled farming haven.

History

The settlement originated during high-medieval forest clearings and was first documented around 1350 as Pramperg. The name derives from the Old High German word pram, meaning blackberry, symbolized today by a fruiting blackberry branch in the municipal coat of arms. Brandberg became historically prominent in 1837 as a stronghold of the Zillertal Inclinants: due to their Protestant convictions, numerous farming families were expelled under an imperial decree and forced to emigrate to Silesia. For generations, farmers have painstakingly hand-scythed the mountain hay meadows on slopes angled up to sixty degrees to prevent catastrophic avalanches in winter; these meadows now count among the most biodiverse habitats in the Eastern Alps. A modern connection came in 1983 with the completion of the 2.1-kilometer Brandberg Tunnel, securing year-round road access from Mayrhofen. The Late Baroque Holy Cross Parish Church was constructed between 1786 and 1787, forming a protected historic ensemble alongside its 1715 timber tithe barn.

How to Get There

Motorists travel to Brandberg via the Inntal motorway A12, taking the Zillertal exit and following federal highway B169 up the valley towards Mayrhofen. At the roundabout, a turnoff leads through the 2,130-meter Brandberg Tunnel directly into the village center. Train passengers take the narrow-gauge Zillertalbahn to its terminus in Mayrhofen im Zillertal. From the railway station, regular regional bus route 4100 climbs up to Brandberg village center and Gasthof Thanner.

Tips

A prime historic landmark is the heritage-listed Schrofenmühle watermill dating to 1654, representing the last fully preserved grain mill in the entire Zillertal. Along the Brandberg Cultural Landscape Trail, walkers wander past ancient timber homesteads such as the Hanserhof, established in 1495. A rewarding hike leads up to the traditional Kolmhaus lodge at 1,845 meters, serving regional alpine fare and functioning as the basecamp for summiting the distinctive 2,700-meter Brandberger Kolm peak. Further up the wild Zillergrund valley, visitors can explore the monumental Zillergründl dam reservoir and continue into the tranquil Hohenaualm, affectionately celebrated as the Little Tibet of the Zillertal.
